submissions.findingTextShort: A 2025 single-arm phase-I study gave oral luteolin 50 mg/day for six months to five men under prostate-cancer active surveillance without observed adverse events.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2025 single-arm phase-I study treated five men with low- or intermediate-risk prostate cancer under active surveillance with oral luteolin 50 mg daily for six months and reported no adverse events in the five participants. This is preliminary short-term exposure/tolerability evidence in a tiny disease-specific cohort, not broad population safety proof.
submissions.populationContext: Five men with low- or intermediate-risk prostate cancer under active surveillance
submissions.usageContext: Isolated oral luteolin 50 mg/day for six months
submissions.safetyContext: No adverse events were observed in the five-person phase-I cohort.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small single-arm study; cannot establish uncommon adverse-event rates, long-term safety, or safety in other populations.

submissions.findingTextShort: The available isolated-luteolin human study is phase-I and too small to support broad clinical efficacy claims.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Although the phase-I study examined oncologic and tissue outcomes, its single-arm design and five-person sample make it preliminary feasibility/safety evidence rather than robust clinical efficacy evidence. Mechanistic, preclinical, botanical-combination, or larger combination-product findings should not be used to inflate isolated-luteolin efficacy certainty.
submissions.populationContext: Isolated-luteolin human evidence base represented by a five-person phase-I cohort
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Additional controlled, adequately powered isolated-luteolin trials are needed for proposition-specific efficacy conclusions.
